title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence
excerpt:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing

Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent report...
body_text:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing

Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.

The Republican-led foreign affairs and intelligence committees of the US Congress asked Huang to testify next week at a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” in response to a New York Times report in ​October alleging he ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.

Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.

Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.

The company’s board said in a statement on that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.

“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”

Huang fully ‌supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.

Axios reported on ​Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full ⁠responsibility for his actions.

“I was unfaithful to my ​wife. My ​actions hurt her ​and our children. There is no excuse ​for what ‌I did,” ​Huang said ​in the draft email also seen by Reuters.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.

The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping, China’s president, and seated at the top table with Donald Trump and Xi.

Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.

However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China.

US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.

The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Alice Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.

The investigation also follows a rough few days on Wall Street for AI tech firms, particularly Nvidia. A sell-off of tech stocks that began earlier this month and gained steam with disappointing earnings led to a total decline of nearly $1tn in value off the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in one week and erased about $2tn in a month.

A drop of 3.1% for Nvidia, previously worth about $5tn, whose chips have made it the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward recently.

Robert Mackey, Nick Robins-Early and Blake Montgomery contributed reporting

title: Steve Sarkisian has already started his campaign for Texas Longhorns with ridiculous 'big game' comments

body_text:
"He had said at SEC Media days that essentially semifinals were not good enough anymore. It's got to be a championship game. Those are his words, not mine. "

When SEC programs hire head coaches, a key part of their interview process must be testing their ability to do marketing and promotion.

Few, if any, coaches excel at marketing, like LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin, who has worked tirelessly to convince the broader college football public that losing games should not be punished because of SEC stadiums. Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea campaigned in 2025 by telling fans, voters and media that SEC teams should be given preferential treatment over all other conferences if they have the same records.

SUDDENLY, STEVE SARKISIAN IS SINGING A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT TUNE ABOUT PLAYING OHIO STATE

Head Coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns looks on during the first half against the Tennessee Volunteers at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

The Texas Longhorns head coach said in 2025 that excluding his 9-3 team from the College Football Playoff would be a "disservice to the sport." A disservice! College football would forever be lesser if a 9-3 Texas team was not included, despite several awful performances against a bad Florida team, a bad Mississippi State team, a bad Kentucky team, and getting blown out by Georgia.

Sark complained about the result of the 2025 matchup between the Longhorns and Ohio State Buckeyes hurt his team's resume, saying that even in a 14-7 loss, Texas shouldn't be punished for scheduling a tough opponent. There's some truth to that, sure, but after their miraculous comeback in this year's game, he had a totally different perspective.

"We could be like other teams and play Jones Junior High and win 66-0," he said to reporters after beating OSU. "I don’t know what that does for us. Tonight we found out that we can (win big games)."

When they lose, the result shouldn't matter. When they win, it's a huge boost to their resume compared to teams that played lesser opponents. Shocking.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL FANS AND MEDIA RIP SEC REFS OVER CONTROVERSIAL FORWARD FUMBLE CALL IN TEXAS-MISSOURI GAME

Well, Sark is back, and this time, the marketing effort is to convince those watching that the Longhorns are actually humble little "nobody believes in us" underdogs. Against Missouri.

"I'm really proud of our football team overall because our guys, they're not naive to noise. As much as I would love to say, tune it all out — and we try our best to do that — I could hear the talk getting on the plane yesterday. I could hear the talk when we got here," he said after their 34-20 win. "Nobody believed we'd win the game. Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage. Everyone thought we'd be pushed around."

He continued, saying that the "DNA" of Texas is "toughness," which showed through against the Tigers.

"The DNA of this organization is mental and physical toughness, and I think that poured out of our pores today in this ball game today, and so I'm very proud of them for that. I'm very proud of the way they hung together, the way they responded to adversity," Sarkisian said.

And finally, claimed that the win showed they're "big game hunters."

"We are big game hunters, and we showed up again today," he added.

Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian walks into Camping World Stadium ahead of the Citrus Bowl against the Michigan Wolverines in Orlando, Fla., on Dec. 31, 2025. (aAustin American-Statesman via Getty Images)

Sure! It was a good win for Texas, on the road against a solid, top-25 level opponent. They did face some "adversity," mainly falling behind after a shaky first quarter, then fighting their way back. But acting as though Texas, literally Texas, with arguably the most expensive roster in the sport, or at worst, top 2-3, is a "nobody believed in us" team is ridiculous. Beyond ridiculous.

Texas also had some help, well, a lot of help from the officials. A number of questionable calls went against the Tigers, including what appeared to be a completed pass on a big third down deep in Texas territory, and what seemed like a clear incomplete pass from Arch Manning on 3rd-and-10 being ruled a fumble that gave the Longhorns a 12-yard gain and a first down. Sure enough, that drive resulted in a touchdown and what wound up being 21 unanswered points.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

That's not to say officiating was the reason Texas won, but it sure didn't hurt. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz implied as much after the game, when asked about the number of calls that went against his team.

"If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not going to do that. I'm not going to blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach Sarkisian and his team," he said, according to On3.

Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian pauses during the second half against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, on Nov. 22, 2025. (Scott Wachter/Imagn Images)

Even the announcing team, including Jesse Palmer, were flabbergasted at the officiating.

"If you're a Missouri fan, if you're Eli Drinkwitz, you are livid because it does feel like a lot of these calls are going against Missouri today," he said.

Again, this isn't to say Texas didn't deserve to win, they outplayed Missouri on the field and were the better team. It's the attitude that Sarkisian brings, that they were just humble underdogs clinging to a win against the big, bad Missouri Tigers that's the marketing campaign.

By acting as though every win his team gets is a monumental achievement, it builds the case that should Texas trip up against, say, a struggling LSU or on the road against a bad Texas A&M team, they can't be punished for it. It's marketing. It's classic SEC. And it's ridiculous.

title: JJ McCarthy left Giants game with hip injury, putting Jameis Winston in the lineup but that isn't whole story

body_text:
Drew Brees and Adam Amin break down the WILD ending of the New Orleans Saints' Week 6 win against the New York Giants, along with why J.J. McCarthy's late-game performance could raise questions about the team's QB1 moving forward.

J.J. McCarthy had two basic issues during his time with the Minnesota Vikings: Ability. And durability.

Since his trade to the New York Giants, McCarthy has shown no ability problems because he beat out Jameis Winston as the team's starter and even provided something of a spark in helping New York beat the Houston Texans in overtime.

New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) throws a pass during a game between the New York Giants and the Houston Texans in Houston, TX. ..Trask Smith/CSM/Sipa USA (Credit Image: © Trask Smith/Cal Sport Media/Sipa USA) (Trask Smith/Cal Sport Media/Sipa USA)

McCarthy left the game against the Philadelphia Eagles with what the team is saying is a hip injury.

PATRICK MAHOMES SUFFERS APPARENT ELBOW INJURY ON THROWING ARM BUT RETURNS TO FACE THE NEW YORK JETS

So, back to Jameis Winston for the Giants.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) warms up before a game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images (Troy Taormina-Imagn Images)

Winston entered the game on the Giants’ first possession of the third quarter after McCarthy took a shot from Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. McCarthy gingerly got himself to the New York sideline and took a knee.

McCarthy tried to throw a warmup pass after collecting himself and could be seen writhing in pain during the follow-through.

OutKick and FOX News Digital medical expert said the tape of the play suggests an oblique muscle injury. The Giants say McCarthy is questionable to return. .

McCarthy completed 9 of 13 passes for 101 yards before he departed. He was sacked five times in the first half.

New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston gets a hug from Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy prior to an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals in East Rutherford, N.J., on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

He returned to the sideline and was seen encouraging his teammates as if he intended to return to the game.

Despite what appeared to be too much pain to function, McCarthy returned to the game in the fourth quarter. It is possible he agreed to take a shot to deaden the pain and return.

title: Dunleavy calls Alaska voting system ‘very confusing’ as razor-thin Senate race frozen in time
excerpt: The Alaska Senate race remains undecided as Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola are separated by fewer than 700 votes. Finn and Dunleavy discuss the impact of same-name candidate Da...
body_text:
The Alaska Senate race remains undecided as Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola are separated by fewer than 700 votes. Finn and Dunleavy discuss the impact of same-name candidate Dan J. Sullivan, who received thousands of votes, as the closely watched race remains unresolved.

Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy admits his own state's voting system is "very confusing," and warned that the close race between Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola and incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan will not be determined for days, if not weeks.

"It's very close, the numbers," Dunleavy told WABC Radio's "The Cats Roundtable" on Sunday, noting key dates for ballot dumps will be Friday, Nov. 13, and Wednesday, Nov. 18, when "another big batch of votes will come in."

"It's a slow system up here in Alaska," he admitted, acknowledging that "we've got quite a quite an issue up here."

"A big batch of votes will come and that'll really determine, you know, who's going to have the lead."

ALASKA, MISSISSIPPI SENATE RACES SEPARATED BY RAZOR-THIN VOTE MARGINS

Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, and Democrat Senate-nominee Mary Peltola are locked in a race too close to call that has the challenger leading by just 637 votes. (Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Peltola, currently with 48.17% support, leads by just 637 votes in Alaska's ranked-choice voting system that has not dropped any new vote tallies for days. Election Day was Tuesday, Nov. 3 and if no candidate gets 50% support as the No. 1 choice by Nov. 25, the results to go to rounds of ranked-choice candidates on the second and third choices.

"It is very confusing," Dunleavy said. "That was also on the ballot, to actually repeal that voting scheme that was put in place here just a couple years ago, and so it's confusing, 100%."

ALASKA VOTER 'DISGUSTED' BY REPORTED 'DECOY DAN' PLOT SWITCHES FROM PELTOLA TO SULLIVAN

"No" votes against repealing ranked-choice voting lead very narrowly at 51.85%. That decision also remains too close to call a week after the polls closed.

"We're still in the process of bringing in votes and counting votes," Dunleavy said. "And we are in the midst of investigations as to determine if there was any wrongdoing, especially anything that might resemble perjury or, you know, a misrepresentation of individual's intent on how they wanted their candidacy to be placed on the ballot."

TRUMP ADMIN PUTS ALLEGED 'DECOY DAN' CONSPIRATORS ON NOTICE IN ALASKA ELECTION SPOILER PROBE

Dunleavy denounced what he called the "Decoy Dan" scheme that had Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot in an alleged plot to siphon votes from the Republican incumbent.

The governor claime that other Sullivan even allegedly tried to get on the general election ballot as Daniel S. Sullivan, using the middle initial of the incumbent instead of his own.

EX-ALASKA LAWMAKER DETAILS MYSTERY RECRUITER AS FBI, CONGRESS WIDEN 'DECOY DAN' SCRUTINY

"That kind of opened our eyes and we began an investigation back there, the division of elections did, to determine if this was a legitimate candidacy, and the division of elections at that time found that was not and did not put him on the ballot," Dunleavy said. "Then there was a court case and the Supreme Court in the end ruled against the division of elections in Alaska and they must go on the ballot."

After a New York Times report tied potential knowledge of the "Decoy Dan" scheme on behalf of Peltola's campaign, Dunleavy reopened the investigation of wrongdoing.

"When The New York Times article came out, you know, we already knew a lot of what was happening there, but there was more revelations of that article," he said. "As a result of that, we began another investigation up here in Alaska, and the Department of Justice did the same, so you have this investigation going on right in the middle of an election."

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Riot breaks out at influencer boxing event attended by Tommy Robinson in Ireland
excerpt:
Two people arrested after Robinson’s presence inflames tensions in scenes witnessed by many on social media

Two people were arrested at an influencer boxing event that descended into a riot in Irelan...
body_text:
Two people arrested after Robinson’s presence inflames tensions in scenes witnessed by many on social media

Two people were arrested at an influencer boxing event that descended into a riot in Ireland after the presence of the far-right activist Tommy Robinson inflamed tensions in the crowd.

The riot took place at about midnight on Saturday at an event organised by the controversial internet personality HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, at the Hub events venue in Kilkenny.

Robinson, 43, is on bail after being found guilty in October of harassing two journalists to the point it caused them fear of violence. He is due back in court on 16 December for a sentencing hearing, with a substantial custodial sentence possible.

Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, was a ringside guest and surrounded by a number of his supporters at the event, which was organised by Sullivan and fellow internet personality Ed Matthews under their Unhinged events company. Sullivan and Matthews earlier this year featured in a Netflix documentary about manosphere influencers. On Friday, Sullivan told the Guardian that Robinson would be attending the event.

A chaotic and violent press conference on Friday evening was a sign of the disorder to come, with competitors repeatedly attacking each other. They included streamers, fitness personalities, drill rappers, OnlyFans models, and Paul Flaherty, a convicted sex offender turned YouTuber.

The event, which was livestreamed on the Kick platform to about 1.8 million viewers, began without incident. The atmosphere grew tense when Sullivan and Matthews invited Robinson to the commentator’s desk before a fight by the Muslim social media personality Mo Deen, whose real name is Mohammad Kubba.

Robinson, who was holding a copy of his book The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, told Matthews that “Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years”, and cited false statistics about Muslim men and sexual offences. Many of the racially diverse people at the event took offence at Robinson’s comments.

After Kubba won his fight he climbed out of the ring and jumped on to Robinson, throwing punches. A scuffle was brought under control by security, with further competitive fights set to resume.

However, the event erupted into a riot after Sullivan demanded that Kubba, who had left the event, return to “face off” against Robinson in the ring. A reluctant Kubba was escorted back into the venue by the event’s security team. It appeared that Sullivan wished for the pair to have an unscheduled bareknuckle fight, with Sullivan repeatedly heard saying “let Tommy fight him”. Sullivan also allowed Robinson’s entourage, whom he referred to as “Tommy’s boys”, into the ring.

Upon Kubba’s arrival in the ring, which by now was filled with Robinson’s supporters, Robinson threw a copy of his book, which has Arabic-style lettering, at Kubba, and a fight broke out. The crowd erupted into violence, with chairs and barricades being thrown and attenders punching each other, as others screamed and ran for safety.

Interviewed by the Guardian after the riot, Kubba claimed he had been told to start a fight with Robinson, although he declined to say by whom. Before the fight began, Robinson had said he would be willing to “batter” Kubba if the Muslim personality started a fight with him, although he also said that he liked Kubba and bore no ill will towards him. There is no suggestion the riot was pre-planned.

Over the next 20 minutes violent scenes unfolded, as Sullivan pleaded unsuccessfully with the crowd to stay peaceful. The riot was eventually broken up by event and venue security and the gardaí, who had been called to the venue earlier in the night after disturbances.

A Garda Síochána spokesperson confirmed that a male in his 30s was assaulted and removed from the scene to St Luke’s hospital in Kilkenny, while another male in his 20s was arrested and detained at a police station. A teenage boy was also arrested and subsequently charged with violent disorder, and was due to appear in court on Sunday.

Footage of the riot spread on social media in real time. Before the live stream cut to black, some in the crowd could be heard chanting “Oh Tommy Robinson”. After police dispersed the crowds, Sullivan attempted to restart the fights for the live stream only, but was blocked from doing so by a visibly upset representative of the venue.

The Ministry of Justice and the Metropolitan police were unable to confirm whether Robinson’s bail terms prohibited international travel.

In comments uploaded to social media on Sunday, Sullivan acknowledged that he had erred by not hiring more event security. “Everyone makes mistakes when you are trying to grow something,” he said, before adding: “One thing I can say is it was a great night of entertainment and it’s gone super viral.” On its official Instagram account, @unhinged_promotions, footage of the riot was uploaded with the caption: “The Area started a RIOT.”

Outside the venue in the early hours of Sunday morning, the crowd, predominantly teenage boys and young men, filmed the aftermath on their phones. One attender told the Guardian that such things did not happen in Kilkenny city, which has a population of 27,000.

title: Carlos Alcaraz beats Ben Shelton to win Paris Masters tennis title
excerpt:
Carlos Alcaraz has gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man ...
body_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man who ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career on Sunday.

Unlike their five-set quarterfinal epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

“Coming here every year, not finding my best tennis but we never gave up,” Alcaraz said after being handed the trophy for the first time by former Paris Masters winner Boris Becker.

“We had really painful losses here and we always said try again,” the Spaniard  added with a smile.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run from November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year – only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

Coming into Paris on the back of winning the 500-level title in Vienna, Alcaraz has won his last nine matches.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route – this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarterfinals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level – both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
excerpt:
One of two surgeons who treated victims on the streets in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague"undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer.

The pa...
body_text:
One of two surgeons who treated victims on the streets in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague"undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer.

The pair were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15.

The doctors raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator.

On Sunday, the officers - both hailed as "true heroes" by the prime minister for preventing further deaths - emerged from comas.

Prosecutors launched a terror investigation after ministers previously said the 24-year-old Polish attacker - who remains in a critical condition - was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies".

A British national and Austrian woman were among those killed alongside four Poles.

Professor Michal Pędziwiatr and Dr Mateusz Wierdak were having lunch in central Krakow with their families when they heard gunshots, local media reported.

"Suddenly my son ran up and said: 'Dad, they're shooting at people there, people are falling to the ground'," Pędziwiatr told news outlet Fakt.

Pędziwiatr said when they got to the scene, they treated both the apparent attacker and the police officers.

"When it comes to saving lives, it doesn't matter who is who," he added.

Once the shooting stopped, Pędziwiatr said he took care of the other victims and the perpetrator, while Wierdak began working on the police officer who was shot in the chest during the gunfight.

Watch: Professor Michal Pędziwiatr says Dr Mateusz Wierdak is "a hero"

"He, to put it colloquially, stuffed all the bandages into [the police officer's] chest and stuck his hands in," he told Fakt.

"If not for that, I don't know how things would have turned out, as there was a long wait for the ambulance."

Meanwhile, Pędziwiatr said he called John Paul II Hospital where the Department of Thoracic and Cardiac Surgery is located.

"I insisted they take him there because, in my opinion, he had the best chance of survival there, where there were specialists for precisely this type of injury," he told Fakt.

According to local media, Wierdak is a renowned surgeon in Krakow. The University Hospital in Krakow states Pędziwiatr is head of General, Oncological, Metabolic and Emergency Surgery.

The police officers have been identified as senior constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański.

Investigations continued in central Krakow on Sunday before Main Market Square reopened

The attacker has not yet been named by authorities.

When his house was searched after the attack in central Krakow, the bodies of his parents and sister were found.

The National Public Prosecutor's Office in Poland launched an investigation into the attack with a unit specialising in "terrorist offences" taking the lead.

Separately, reports emerged that six Dublin Civil Defence volunteers also assisted in the aftermath of the shooting.

James McConnell, an officer, told RTE News the group were on a city break and were close to the main square, external when the shooting happened.

The volunteers who are trained to provide medical care immediately sought to help injured people, providing "CPR and haemorrhage control".

Witnesses who were close to the attack described panic and confusion around the square as it unfolded.

Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives".

Not knowing where the gunman was - or if there were multiple - they "just kept sprinting", eventually finding a hotel to hide inside.

How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded

Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover".

He continued: "I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away."

The suspect wore full military tactical gear during the attack and was described as having a military-grade weapon - but the government said he was not a member of the Polish armed forces.

Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said "everything suggests" the suspect was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held ultra-nationalist views.

The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) on Saturday in the historic centre of Krakow.

Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out.

The glass front of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes.

The mayor of Krakow said he had submitted an urgent request for the two officers injured while stopping the attacker to be awarded titles of honorary citizens of the city.

Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted.

What we know so far after Krakow gun attack

Wounded police officers 'saved many lives'

'I saw ambulances and armed police': BBC correspondent in Krakow

Moment police officer appears to shoot Krakow suspect

title: Lisa Nandy wary of ‘circular arguments’ about rejoining EU
excerpt:
Culture secretary pushes back against talk of revisiting Brexit but says closer ties would fulfil referendum promises

One of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said she wants to avoid “circular arg...
body_text:
Culture secretary pushes back against talk of revisiting Brexit but says closer ties would fulfil referendum promises

One of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said she wants to avoid “circular arguments” about whether the UK should rejoin the EU, underlining divisions at the top of government over revisiting Brexit.

Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, appeared to suggest she was not in favour of rejoining the trade bloc, but she said the prime minister should still pursue closer ties to fulfil the promises made at the time of the referendum.

She is one of a handful of cabinet ministers who are concerned about Burnham’s plan for an “honest conversation” with the public about Brexit and who are privately warning it could reopen a row that would only benefit Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.

“I do not believe that anybody wants to repeat circular arguments about in or out, leave or remain. I do think, though, that over the last decade we have let the British people down very badly,” she told the BBC’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme.

Nandy, whose Wigan seat voted overwhelmingly for leave in 2016, and who is one of the most cautious in the cabinet about reversing Brexit, was asked if she wanted to go back in. “I don’t know if that’s a choice we have,” she said.

However, she did concede that Burnham was trying to address the failings of the Brexit deal, telling Sky News it was important to “be honest” and highlight that “the deal that we got is not what we were promised”.

The culture secretary stressed there were “trade-offs and choices” to be made which involved a conversation with people across the country, indicating that Brexit would be a key theme of the next election campaign.

Burnham will attend the European Political Community summit in Dublin on Thursday. Downing Street sources said he would use it to get Labour’s reset deal over the line and to meet many European leaders for the first time.

In private, EU counterparts will be expecting Burnham to set out his ambitions for further integration after he announced his intention to move beyond Labour’s “red lines” on the bloc after the next election.

At a Brexit reset meeting on 20 November in Brussels, agreements on agriculture and food, emissions trading and youth experience visas are expected to be confirmed.

Burnham said at the weekend there was more to come. “This summit will show what we can achieve when we work together, but it doesn’t need to be the end of our ambition,” he told the Sunday Mirror.

Officials will also discuss the agenda for the next round of the reset, which could include another attempt for the UK to join the EU’s €150bn (£125bn) Safe defence fund, collaboration on law enforcement and borders, and visas for touring artists.

Soon after the Brussels summit, Burnham is expected to give a speech setting out options for a closer relationship with the EU, arguing it would be in the UK’s long-term interest. No 10 sources said he wanted to “frame the conversation, not go straight to the endgame” before testing public opinion.

Senior government figures say Burnham wants a mandate to start negotiations with the EU in Labour’s next election manifesto, but that any subsequent referendum would be solely confirmatory.

“You can’t ask people to vote on an undefined plan like in 2016. That was David Cameron’s mistake,” one said.

However, Burnham has faced reservations from others within his cabinet. The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, and home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, are cautious about pushing to fully rejoin.

The EU’s former chief Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier said London could not have the “single market à la carte” by cherrypicking which of the four freedoms – including freedom of movement – it would like in future negotiations.

“There is no cherrypicking. There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other,” he told the BBC.

Nandy was forced to reject allegations that celebrating the UK rejoining the Erasmus plus scheme by linking it to Remembrance Sunday was inappropriate, after suggesting it would help to honour “the immense courage of those who served our country” before Remembrance Sunday.

Kevin Hollinrake, the Tory chair, suggested she was using the national civic occasion to “try to make an EU membership pitch”. He said: “Our veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme.”

Speaking on Sky News, Nandy responded: “They are the only party that is talking about Brexit and the EU. What we are announcing this weekend is that we’re going to widen the Erasmus scheme.

“I cannot see what is political about saying that we want young people from every part of this country to understand the contribution that their grandparents and great-grandparents made, not just to us but to many, many lives of people that they had never met,” she added.

title: Fast-food chain that once lit up American roads still missed decades later
excerpt: Capri Cafaro of Ohio, a culinary storyteller and managing director of America the Bountiful Media, discusses the rise and fall of bygone restaurant chain The Red Barn and how its memory lives on today...
body_text:
Capri Cafaro of Ohio, a culinary storyteller and managing director of America the Bountiful Media, discusses the rise and fall of bygone restaurant chain The Red Barn and how its memory lives on today.

With its distinctive barn-shaped buildings and menu of burgers, fried chicken and other American classics, Red Barn was a pioneer in the fast-food industry.

Founded in 1961 by Don Six, Martin Levine and Jim Kirst, the chain grew to between 300 and 400 restaurants before its final locations closed in 1988, according to numerous sources.

The first Red Barn opened in Ohio, although there's debate over whether Columbus or Springfield is its birthplace.

FAST-FOOD DRIVE-THRUS TOOK OVER AMERICAN MORNINGS FOR THESE KEY REASONS

"I think it's important to note that Ohio is actually a bit of an icon as a state when it comes to being the home of iconic fast-food brands," Capri Cafaro, the Ohio-based managing director of America the Bountiful Media, told Fox News Digital.

Wendy's, founded in Columbus, was one of the first restaurant chains to offer a drive-thru window, Cafaro noted. It also stood apart from the competition with its square hamburger patties.

The Red Barn, a fast-food restaurant chain founded in Ohio in 1961, did not stand the test of time. Its final locations shut down in 1988. (iStock; USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

The roast beef chain Arby's was also founded in Ohio, in Boardman.

The barn-shaped buildings of Red Barn restaurants were key identifiers of the brand, as were their comfortable, homey interiors, Cafaro said.

PIZZA HUT BRINGS BACK VINTAGE VIBES AS FRANCHISEES EMBRACE NOSTALGIC MAKEOVERS

"I think that there is something to be said about matching the aesthetic with the name and making that part of its marketing appeal," Cafaro said of the exteriors.

This "iconic material culture" was "pervasive in fast-food restaurants, not just in places like Red Barn, but places like Long John Silver's or, or even more iconically, Pizza Hut," Cafaro said, referencing the hut-style roofs of classic Pizza Hut restaurants.

Owners James O. Oatsvall Sr., left, and Wendell K. Harris are shown standing outside Nashville's second Red Barn Restaurant as it was getting ready to open to the public on July 8, 1966.  (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

The chain's menu consisted of comfort foods like hamburgers, fried chicken, fish sandwiches and more.

A double-decker burger called the Big Barney was similar to the Big Mac but predated the famous McDonald's item, which wasn't added to the national menu until 1968, according to the company's website.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Like McDonald's, Red Barn also used food-themed cartoon characters used as mascots, including Hamburger Hungry, Chicken Hungry and Big Fish Hungry, with "hungry" sometimes spelled "hungery," according to Tasting Table.

Red Barn is "evocative of nostalgia and for people that grew up with it."

The brand also had a jingle: "When the hungries hit, hit the Red Barn."

Red Barn offered a self-serve salad bar, and some publications say it beat Wendy's to the punch.

The Wendy's website, however, claims it was the first national chain to introduce salad bars, doing so in 1979.

The Wendy's website claims that it was the first chain to introduce a salad bar, although some sources say The Red Barn was the first. (Tim Boyle/Getty Images)

At its peak, there were about 300 to 400 Red Barn locations across 19 U.S. states, Canada and Australia, according to Chowhound.

Many factors can influence a restaurant chain's survival or downfall, Cafaro noted. Red Barn filed for bankruptcy in 1986, according to Tasting Table.

The chain's last 22 locations were in New York, Ohio and Washington, D.C., with the final franchise lease expiring in 1988, Chowhound reported.

A few locations were reborn as independent restaurants with a similar feel to Red Barn, including one in Racine, Wisconsin, called The Farm, which permanently closed in 2020.

At its peak, there were 300 to 400 Red Barn restaurants across America.  (Bob Grannis via Getty Images)

Although not in its original form, The Red Barn still lives on today, with other businesses occupying the recognizable barn-shaped buildings.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Fans of the chain share memories and nostalgic photos in a Facebook group called "I remember The Red Barn Restaurants," which has over 9,000 members.

Red Barn is "evocative of nostalgia and for people that grew up with it," Cafaro said.

But, she added, "it really also does speak to the power of food to evoke nostalgia and memories" and how people "equate food to maybe a happy place."

Sadie Chafe is a writer on the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
excerpt: Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister B...
body_text:
Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his coalition lineup.

In a speech at Sunday’s ceremony in Herzog’s office in Jerusalem, Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join.

“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said.

Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government. At the ceremony, Eisenkot said he will act in the interests of the public and represent all parts of Israeli society.

Herzog, meanwhile, warned that the country faced uncertainties after the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, which brought victories for several political figures critical of Israel and the US’s military support.

“The State of Israel needs a stable government,” Herzog said, pointing to the “new political reality” in the US.

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

Despite this, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate to replace Netanyahu.

In Israel’s October 27 elections, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.

“Netanyahu still has time to derail Gadi Eisenkot’s efforts to form a government and sabotage attempts to gain a vote of confidence,” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank.

“In the meantime, he remains caretaker prime minister. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would be the natural second in line to be tasked with forming a government. And if he fails, elections would then be called, and that would still allow Netanyahu to remain as caretaker.

“Many of Netanyahu’s critics say that is his aim. The big question in Israeli politics now is: does the opposition really want to get rid of Netanyahu? Or is the opposition to Palestinian Israelis in mainstream politics so strong that they’re willing to risk keeping Netanyahu in power by going back to the ballot box?”

title: Fishing is big business, and FXR founder says the sport's growth is only getting started
excerpt:
Bassmaster Elite Series pro Cooper Gallant tells OutKick OutDoors how he got his start in competitive fishing, spent years chasing his dream and refused to consider a

There was a time when catching a...
body_text:
Bassmaster Elite Series pro Cooper Gallant tells OutKick OutDoors how he got his start in competitive fishing, spent years chasing his dream and refused to consider a

There was a time when catching a bass might earn you bragging rights, a fishing trophy or maybe a few bucks from your buddies. On Oct. 31, it earned one Kentucky angler $1.25 million.

Matt Robertson walked away from The Champions on Old Hickory Lake outside Nashville with the richest first-place payout in bass fishing history, capping a three-day tournament that featured a staggering $3.25 million purse and brought together some of the biggest names from Bassmaster and Major League Fishing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

And if the event was any indication, the business of fishing has come a long way from the neighborhood pond.

Matt Robertson celebrates with his catch on stage after winning the 2026 World Bass Enterprises - The Champions Tournament on Oct. 31, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (World Bass Enterprises/Getty Images)

According to the 2026 Special Report on Fishing from the American Sportfishing Association and Outdoor Industry Association, 57 million Americans went fishing at least once in 2025. That's up from 50.1 million in 2019.

Those numbers help explain why companies with roots outside the fishing industry have increasingly turned their attention to the water.

The Canadian company built its reputation making performance apparel for snowmobiling and motorsports. But founder Milt Reimer told OutKick OutDoors that he began recognizing fishing's potential roughly a decade ago, after discovering just how much overlap existed between his motorsports customers and the fishing community.

"We just started to connect through that, and then just realized, man, there is a lot of participation in Minnesota, especially," Reimer said.

Fishing, he explained, was already a summer passion for many of the same people who spent their winters on snowmobiles or their weekends riding dirt bikes.

That connection eventually led FXR into the fishing apparel business, where the company now sponsors several professional anglers including Robertson, Fisher Anaya and 2026 Bassmaster Angler of the Year Trey McKinney.

Trey McKinney, 2026 Bassmaster Angler of the Year, prepares to launch on the final day of The Champions tournament on Old Hickory Lake. (World Bass Enterprises)

But for Reimer, the appeal of fishing extends well beyond the professional tournament circuit.

When asked what an event like The Champions says about the future of the sport, he summed it up pretty definitively: "It's real. It's here. It's in front of us."

Reimer described the adrenaline of a tournament boat launch and the sudden change of pace once anglers reach the water, where wind, current, sunshine and countless other variables determine whether they have a successful day.

It's that combination of competition and connection with the outdoors that he believes resonates with so many people.

And unlike many professional sports, fishing offers a particularly direct connection between the athletes competing at the highest level and the average person who just wants to wet a line after work.

Anglers and boat crews are on the water during day one of the 2026 World Bass Enterprises - The Champions Tournament on Oct. 29, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (World Bass Enterprises/Getty Images)

"There is this massive connection both from the pro side to the regular, just weekend, evening fishermen," Reimer said. "We love that part of it, and we love the community it's building. It helps us to really connect across all our genres of motorsports that we're in, and this is the one core sport that's really generational and passed on in a big way. It really vibes with so many people."

That connection was on full display at The Champions, where 60 competitors from two rival professional circuits went head-to-head for a record-setting payday.

MATT ROBERTSON WINS RECORD $1.25 MILLION FISHING PRIZE, DECLARES 'TRAILER TRASH FOR LIFE'

For Reimer, who had three sponsored anglers in the top 15, the opportunity represented something special.

"It's hard to describe. I'm so jacked for the guys," he said before Saturday's championship round. "It's kind of a dream come true for them."

Matt Robertson prepares to launch on Day 1 of The Champions tournament on Old Hickory Lake. (World Bass Enterprises)

He also praised the tournament for creating a stage where anglers from the sport's two major circuits could compete against one another for a championship.

Robertson ultimately claimed the $1.25 million prize, while McKinney finished fourth and earned $200,000. Anaya finished seventh.

Fisher Anaya out on the water during The Champions bass fishing tournament on Old Hickory Lake. (World Bass Enterprises)

Events like The Champions illustrate just how far professional fishing has come. And with tens of millions of Americans already spending time on the water, there's no shortage of people who can appreciate what these anglers do for a living.

Whether someone is chasing a seven-figure paycheck on a national stage or simply hoping to catch dinner at the local lake, the appeal of fishing remains much the same.

The stakes might be different, but everybody's still waiting for that next bite.

Love all things fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube!

title: Teaching GCSEs early risks turning schools into ‘exam factories’, education secretary warns
excerpt:
Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum

Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools i...
body_text:
Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum

Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education.

Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.

The Department for Education (DfE) said the proposals would be included in the government’s overhaul of the national curriculum to be published in early 2027, as part of its plans to tackle school disengagement as well as the disadvantage gap between pupils from rich and poor backgrounds and the rising number of young people not in education, employment or training.

Powell said: “The early years of secondary school should be a time when children are excited to go to school and engage in the specialist and much broader teaching on offer, and where they find their passion and develop a love of learning.

“Instead, we’ve seen worrying trends of disengagement and high levels of persistent absence, with the disadvantage gap stubbornly large and too many leaving school without the knowledge and skills they need to thrive. That’s what our exciting and engaging new national curriculum aims to address as part of our wider education reforms.

“What’s more, the pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer … and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding. I’m putting a stop to that.”

Many secondary schools start introducing GCSE-level material to pupils in year 9 as a way of spreading out the course content. But Powell told the Sunday Times she was opposed to “early exam factories” and that plans to reduce GCSEs’ content would enable the courses to be taught comfortably within the allotted two years of year 10 and year 11.

The new curriculum will say schools “should not start GCSE specifications early for large cohorts or see children routinely required to narrow their options earlier or entered earlier for exams”, the DfE stated.

However, the new policy will not be compulsory, and schools will retain the flexibility to teach GCSEs to younger students whom they judge to be capable of coping with it.

Powell said slimmed-down GCSEs would give schools “more time to develop deeper understanding, as well as a richer experience that will engage more young people in their passions and prepare them better for the fast-changing world they will grow up in.”

title: Detroit Lions wear Jack Campbell jerseys ahead of Miami Dolphins game to honor injured teammate

The Detroit Lions have gone from crying about Jack Campbell to using the unfortunate injury to their linebacker and defensive team captain as part of their culture for the remainder of the 2026 season.

One week after Campbell was removed on an immobilization stretcher and cart from the field during the game against the Minnesota Vikings, the Lions are reporting for work in South Florida for the game against the Miami Dolphins wearing Campbell jerseys.

About half-a-dozen players wore Campbell's No. 46 jersey to the game.

AWFUL SCENE AS LEO CHANEL SUFFERS NECK INJURY, MARKING SECOND STRAIGHT WEEK WASHINGTON COMMANDERS SUFFER SCARE

Even some players who did not wear the Campbell jersey paid tribute to their teammate somehow.

Aidan Hutchinson carried the gallon jug marked "Jack" into the stadium as a tribute to his fallen teammate.

Hutchinson was in some ways the face of how the Lions reacted when Campbell suffered a serious neck injury during Detroit’s victory over Minnesota last Sunday.

Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell is injured against the Minnesota Vikings during the second half of an NFL game Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Rey Del Rio)

The edge rusher was seen crying as trainers and doctors attended to Campbell as he lay motionless on the turf.

TEARS FROM TEAMMATES AS IMMOBILIZED DETROIT LIONS LINEBACKER JACK CAMPBELL CARTED OFF FIELD AND HOSPITALIZED

This week has been about "playing like 46," for the Lions.

"This is for him, man," fellow linebacker Derrick Barnes told reporters. "One of our keys to victory is preparing to play like No. 46.

"Jack's a fighter, we all know Jack. Knowing Jack, he wants us to keep going throughout our day. That's why we all love Jack. To hear that from coach (Wednesday) morning was awesome."

Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell is taken off the field due to injury against the Minnesota Vikings during the second half of an NFL game Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Paul Sancya)

One of the people wearing No. 46 jerseys on Sunday was defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, who explained what it means to prepare and play like Campbell.

"Every meeting I told the unit, every walkthrough, every play, you all know how Jack prepares. You all know how he plays," Sheppard said. "The way you honor him is to wipe those tears from your eyes and make sure we prepare and play like him."

Trainers tend to Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell after an injury during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit, Mich., on Nov. 1, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)
